metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully merged all 5 .txt files into concat.docx on Desktop using VS Code terminal and LibreOffice Writer, set font size to 10, and saved as .docx format.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use VS Code terminal to concatenate files, open LibreOffice Writer, select all text, change font size, save as .docx via Save As dialog, navigate file system.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests styling capabilities by requiring both font family change (Arial) and a different font size (14), adding complexity to the original font-size-only task.
metadata.explanation: Task requires merging all .txt files into a styled docx. Evaluator checks: (1) all 5 files content present, (2) font size is 14, (3) font name is Arial.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads docx file, extracts full text, unique font sizes (pt), and unique font names using python-docx.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses rules dict keys (required_snippets, expected_font_size, expected_font_name).
All 3 instruction requirements are covered: content merge (0.34), font size (0.33), font name (0.33).

Font name check uses any() instead of all(), meaning it would pass even if only one run uses Arial while others use a different font. The instruction says 'Set the font to Arial' implying ALL text should be Arial. Should use all() like the font size check.
Getter only collects explicitly set font properties (run.font.size/name). Runs inheriting styles from paragraph or document defaults will be skipped, potentially missing improperly styled text.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change font name check from any() to all() to ensure ALL text uses Arial, consistent with the font size check logic: 'if font_names and all(expected_font_name in fn for fn in font_names)'
Consider also checking paragraph-level or document-level default font properties in the getter, not just run-level, to catch inherited styles that may differ from the expected font.
